traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are fully implemented.
The require-test-traceability rule exposes configuration options exactly as specified (autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, testSupportsTemplate) and marks itself as fixable. Helper functions implement safe, non-semantic auto-fix behavior: - For missing file-level @supports, a placeholder JSDoc block with clear TODO guidance is inserted at the top of test files when autoFixTestTemplate is enabled, matching the story’s template and safety requirements. - For malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes, the rule normalizes spacing, delimiters, parentheses, underscores, and casing only when a recognizable REQ identifier is already present, and only for string-literal test names. If no canonicalization is possible or if there is no prefix at all, it reports an error without attempting a fix, satisfying the no-inference and safety constraints.
Tests in tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts explicitly cover all key auto-fix scenarios (missing @supports template insertion and the various malformed prefix formats) and assert exact before/after strings, ensuring behavior aligns with the story. The user documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md documents both the auto-fix capabilities and the template behavior, referencing Story 021.0 directly.
Given the passing Jest test suite and the clear mapping from code and tests back to all REQ-TEST-FIX-* requirements, this story is assessed as PASSED.
